title: Help tells owners a payment link puts money in their account, but payment links are in test mode for every gym
what: The live help article on online payments tells every owner to paste their Razorpay or Cashfree keys, make a payment link, and that the money goes straight to their account. The payments switch in the repo is off, and while it is off every payment-company connection is test mode: no real money moves. The article mentions test mode only as a side note, not as the state of every gym today.
expected: The help says payment links take real money only when that is true, or the payment-link part of the article waits for the switch like the join-and-pay article does. The UPI QR part can stay.
who: owners who read the help or ask the AI help about online payments
how_often: every time, while payments stay in test mode
fix_line: Hold the payment-link half of the article behind the live-payments switch, or say plainly that payment links are in test mode for now

title: Help says member messages are deleted after 180 days, but they are only deleted when someone next opens the list
what: The help tells owners that member messages are deleted 180 days after the last one. No timed job does this. Old messages are removed only at the moment the member opens their messages or someone at the gym opens Member messages. If nobody opens either, the old messages stay.
expected: Messages older than 180 days are removed on a schedule, whoever opens the app, or the help says what really happens.
who: members and owners of a gym where nobody opens the messages for a while
how_often: only at gyms that stop opening messages
fix_line: Add the 180-day clean-up to a daily job (database change, needs his yes), or soften the help line

title: A help library is named in the notes but not found in code
what: The notes at the top of the help articles say the articles feed two things: the AI help answers and the help library. Only the AI answer and the no-AI help-page answer read the articles. No screen in the admin app, the member app or HQ lets a person browse the help pages.
expected: A help library people can browse exists, or the notes stop naming one.
who: nobody yet (inside note only)
how_often: always
fix_line: Decide: build a browse-the-help page, or remove the words from the notes

title: Staff help names a question and choices that are not on the Add a person form
what: The help says to pick Owner or Staff under a question called What can they do. The form really asks What is their job, with four choices: Owner, Staff (front desk), Trainer and Other. The help also says the sign-in code works for a few minutes; the screen says 30 minutes.
expected: The help uses the words on the form and names all four choices, including Trainer.
who: owners adding staff or a trainer
how_often: every time they follow the help
fix_line: Rewrite the step with the real question, the four choices and 30 minutes

title: Diet plan help names a button that does not exist
what: The help says to tap Start from a sample when making a diet plan. The button on the screen reads Start from a ready-made plan. The AI Assistant itself tells owners to start from a ready plan.
expected: The help names the button as it is written on the screen.
who: owners and trainers making a diet plan
how_often: every time they follow the help
fix_line: Change the help words to Start from a ready-made plan

title: Your growth help says old numbers can be typed in, but the button opens the Excel import
what: The help says to use Add old records to type your old numbers. The button opens the import page, which takes an Excel or CSV file of old members and fee records; nothing is typed. The button also shows only while the gym has no older records, which the help does not say.
expected: The help says Add old records brings in an Excel or CSV file, and that the button goes away once old records are in.
who: owners comparing with the time before MettleUp
how_often: every time they follow the help
fix_line: Reword the step: Add old records opens Import from Excel

title: No automatic check that the buttons named in help exist on the screens
what: The help file's own rule is never to name a button that is not in the code, checked by hand on 4 Nov 2026. The test file checks ids, length, banned words and that every screen has an article, but compares button names with the screens for the messaging articles only. Three articles have already drifted (staff, diet plans, Your growth).
expected: A test fails when a quoted button or label in a help article is not found in the screen code.
who: anyone reading help or an AI help answer after a screen's words change
how_often: each time a screen is reworded
fix_line: Add a test that searches the app code for every quoted label in the help articles

title: Notes say steps and water each day will be built, but no water log exists
what: The backlog decided to build steps and water each day. Steps today exists (read from Health Connect). No place to log water was found in the member app.
expected: A water log exists, or the backlog says water was dropped.
who: members
how_often: every time
fix_line: Build a simple water log or mark water as dropped in the backlog

title: Notes plan a join-by-email match, but it is not in the app
what: The backlog says a member who signs in with Google is offered their gym when the email matches the gym's member list. The add-member form has an email box, but nothing in the member app or the server looks a gym up by email.
expected: The match exists, or the backlog says it is still only a plan.
who: members joining a gym
how_often: every time
fix_line: Keep it as a plan in the backlog, or build the match with the ask-first step

title: Notes say register photos come later for the AI import; nothing reads a photo
what: The AI import plan names two inputs: an Excel or CSV file now, photos of a paper register later, with a price per photo. The import takes files only, and the AI part only matches column names.
expected: Photo import exists, or the backlog shows it as not built.
who: owners with paper registers
how_often: every time
fix_line: Mark photo import as not built in the backlog, or plan it

title: HQ plan lists export of a gym's data, but HQ only exports the list of gyms
what: The HQ plan, marked done, lists export a gym's data among its actions. HQ has one export: the list of gyms as a CSV of gym facts. No action hands over one gym's records.
expected: HQ can export one gym's data, or the plan says the gym downloads its own backup instead.
who: HQ admin
how_often: when a gym asks for its data
fix_line: Decide if the gym's own download backup is enough, and correct the plan

title: Five ideas named in the notes are not in the app, as the owner decided
what: The notes name a gym-only feed, compare with a friend, stronger than X% of your gym, a gym step challenge and counting reps by listening. The same notes park the first four and cancel the last. None was found in the code, which matches the decision.
expected: Nothing to build. The feature list should show them as parked so nobody counts them as missing.
who: nobody
how_often: never
fix_line: Mark these five as parked in the feature list

title: Website says our staff cannot open a member list unless the gym lets them in, but HQ can open it in an emergency
what: The gym-owner site says: closed to our staff, they cannot open your member list unless you let them in for 1 hour. HQ has an emergency action that opens read-only access to any gym for 15 to 60 minutes with a typed reason and no OK from the gym. It is logged and the owner sees it afterwards.
expected: The website line also names the logged emergency access, or the emergency action needs the gym's OK.
who: gym owners reading the website
how_often: every time
fix_line: Add the emergency case to the website line, in approved words

title: Desk still has Check workout code, but the member app no longer shows a code
what: The notes say the member app shows Show my workouts to the desk with a short code that the desk types in. That screen was removed from the member app on 2 Nov 2026. The member page in the admin app still shows the Check workout code button, so staff can ask for a code no member can produce.
expected: The desk button is removed, or the member app shows the code again.
who: desk staff and owners
how_often: every time they open a member page
fix_line: Remove the Check workout code button and its sheet from the admin app

title: Notes say Google Drive stays as an extra copy for people who want one; the app can no longer back up to Drive
what: The decision of 24 Oct says workouts go to our server and Google Drive becomes an extra copy only for people who want one. In the app a member can only bring back an old Drive backup. The code that uploads a new Drive backup is still there, but no screen calls it.
expected: Members who want a Drive copy can make one, or the notes say Drive backup was retired.
who: members who want their own copy
how_often: every time
fix_line: Confirm Drive backup is retired and remove the unused upload code, or bring the choice back

title: Notes say the free limits can be switched on from HQ with no app update; the switch is built into the app
what: The plan says members without a gym get limits (4 routines, 7 own exercises, 3 months of charts) that stay off at launch and are switched on from the owner panel with no app update. The paid-features switch is a fixed value inside the app, so turning it on needs a new app version. The limits also differ: no limit on the number of routines was found.
expected: The switch can be flipped from HQ, or the notes say a release is needed and list the real limits.
who: the owner, later members without a gym
how_often: once, when paid features start
fix_line: Read the switch from the server, or plan a release for the day it turns on

title: HQ plan says it shows app versions; the card says not connected yet
what: The HQ plan lists app versions among the things HQ shows. HQ shows how many times each release was downloaded, but the card Which app version members use only says it is not connected yet.
expected: The card shows which versions members run, or it is removed until it can.
who: HQ admin
how_often: every time
fix_line: Remove the empty card or connect it

title: Notes say nothing locks when a free trial ends; a staged lock is built behind a switch that is off
what: The free-trial decision says: when a trial ends, nothing locks. That is true today. The admin app also holds a built stop-paying path (7 extra days, then 30 days of basics only with no new members, then look and download only) that also covers a trial that ended. It is behind the plan switch, which is off. The trial banner's own notes still say nothing is ever locked.
expected: One rule for what happens after a trial ends, written the same in the notes, the banner and the lock.
who: gym owners after their trial
how_often: once the plan switch goes on
fix_line: Decide the rule before the switch goes on and align the banner words with it

title: Notes say feedback can be typed or spoken in both apps; the admin app only takes typing
what: The feedback plan says a Send feedback button in the member app and the admin app, type or speak. The member app has speak. The admin app's Help and feedback page has a typing box only; speaking exists there only inside the AI Assistant.
expected: The admin app's feedback takes voice too, or the plan says typing only for owners.
who: owners and desk staff
how_often: every time
fix_line: Add the speak button to the admin feedback box or drop it from the plan

title: The backlog calls a location check at the QR scan worth building, but nothing of it exists
what: The note of 29 Oct says a fixed QR poster lets a member check in from anywhere, and answers that a one-time location check (within about 150 m of a pin the owner drops) is worth it and takes 2 to 3 days. No pin, no location permission and no at-the-gym mark were found in the member app, the admin app or the gym server. So a photo of the poster still earns challenge days and workout-offer rewards from home.
expected: Either the location check is built, or the note says it is parked and why, and challenge rewards are known to rest on the plain QR.
who: gym owners who give rewards for visits
how_often: every check-in made away from the gym
fix_line: Decide: build the location check for reward check-ins, or park it in writing

title: Class booking is on the backlog as waiting for the gym visit, and is still not built
what: The backlog lists class booking (timetable, spaces left, book and cancel) as a gap against the gym's old software, waiting for the question "Do you run group classes?". Only one-to-one personal-training booking exists, and that sits behind a server part. No group class timetable or booking was found on any surface.
expected: The gym visit question is answered and class booking is either planned or dropped in writing.
who: gyms that run group classes
how_often: every time such a gym compares us with its old software
fix_line: Ask the gym the group-class question, then plan or drop class booking

title: The price decision still lists a Pro + AI pack that the product has since retired
what: The decided price list of 30 Oct has three packs, the third being Pro + AI at 2,499 rupees a month. The shared pack list now says that pack was retired on 12 Nov and replaced by AI credits on every plan; nothing sells or shows it. The decision note was never corrected, so anyone reading it gets a price list that no longer exists.
expected: The price decision names only what is sold today: Starter, Pro, AI credits, the founding offer.
who: the owner and anyone pricing from the note
how_often: every time the note is read
fix_line: Add one line to the price decision saying Pro + AI became AI credits on 12 Nov

title: The switching offer in the price plan (pay nothing until the old software's year ends) is nowhere on the website
what: The price plan the owner picked includes an offer for gyms moving from their old software: free move of records, set-up in person, and no payment until their paid year ends, up to 6 months. The website's price section only says 3 free months for everyone and half price for extra branches. No switching offer, and no way in HQ to give a longer free period by offer, was found in the price list code.
expected: The offer is on the website and the sales material, or the note says it was dropped.
who: gym owners who already paid another software for the year
how_often: every such prospect
fix_line: Decide if the switching offer still stands; if yes, add it to the price section

title: Online acceptance of the terms is live, but its own server file still says it was never switched on
what: The backlog says owners accept the terms with a tick box at Create my gym, live on the server since 24 Oct. The live database does have the two functions that keep and read an acceptance (checked in the function list today). The server file that made them still opens with the words NOT APPLIED, needs the owner's yes, and the feature list carries it as unknown because of that line.
expected: The file's first line says when it went live, like the other live server parts.
who: anyone deciding what is live from the server files
how_often: every time the file is read
fix_line: Change the first line of the terms server file to say it is live since 24 Oct

title: The complaints contact was promised in both apps, but the member app shows no way to reach it after joining
what: The launch task says the named contact for data complaints goes into the privacy notice and both apps. In the member app the privacy notice is linked only inside the tick box shown once at sign-in or when joining a gym. Settings and About show credits and the version only: no privacy notice, no terms, no contact address. A member who wants to complain about their data later has nowhere in the app to find who to write to.
expected: Settings or About in the member app has a Privacy and terms row that shows the contact name and address.
who: every member
how_often: every time a member looks for the privacy notice or the complaints contact
fix_line: Add a Privacy and terms row with the contact to the member app's About page

title: The data agreement says every look at a gym's records is recorded and shown in the admin app, but direct database looks are not shown and may not be recorded
what: The data agreement for gyms and the MettleUp access card both tell the owner that every look is recorded and listed in the admin app. The admin app lists only looks made through a support window. Looks made straight in the database with the owner login are sent by the server in a separate list that the admin app never reads or shows. The notes say this list is not built, that the recording stays off until a logs key is saved in HQ, and that a look made with the server key is never recorded at all.
expected: Every kind of look is recorded and the owner can see it in the admin app, or the agreement and the card say exactly which looks are listed.
who: every gym owner who accepted the data agreement
how_often: every direct look at gym data
fix_line: Show the direct looks in the MettleUp access card and confirm the logs key is saved, or narrow the sentence in the agreement and the card

title: The admin app says a member gets the automatic birthday wish when the member's phone may never show it
what: With the automatic birthday wish on, the AI Assistant and Today stop asking the owner to wish a member whose mobile number and first name match an app member, and say that member gets the wish at 9:30 am. The wish is a notification the member's own phone sets for itself. It does not show when the member turned off reminders from the gym, has notifications off, or has not opened the app lately. The notes also name an older case: a number that was typed but never proven counts as wished in the admin app while the server refuses it. In all these cases nobody wishes the member.
expected: The admin app counts a member as wished only when the wish will really reach them, or the words say the wish is set on the member's phone and may be switched off there.
who: members with a birthday whose phone has gym reminders or notifications off, and their gym owner
how_often: each birthday of such a member
fix_line: Soften the admin app words to say the wish is set on the member's phone, or have the phone tell the server whether gym reminders are on

title: What's new tells members silent gym messages and Rest is over now make a sound, but this was never proven on a real phone of that kind
what: The 0.79.0 What's new line says that on some phones gym messages and Rest is over made no sound and now they do. The notes say the ring was not proven on the owner's OPPO, the only phone known to have the fault; the cloud test phone keeps its sounds, so it proves only that nothing rings twice. The notes also say the buzz and the pop-up banner are still missing on those phones. The line is live in open testing.
expected: The line is shown only after the ring is heard on a real phone that had the fault, and it does not suggest the buzz or the pop-up came back.
who: members on OPPO and OnePlus phones
how_often: every gym message and every rest end on those phones, if the fix does not work there
fix_line: Test a gym reply and a locked-screen rest end on the owner's OPPO with 0.79.0 before production; drop the line if it stays silent

title: Dragging an exercise up in a live workout sometimes drops it at the bottom of the list
what: In the release test rounds for 0.79.0, on the owner-size test phone, an exercise held and dragged up above another one landed at the bottom of the list in 2 of 5 runs. The notes call it an open app question with no cause found and say it looks new in 0.79.0. The suspected part is the rule that moves the held card by the gap between where the list is scrolled and where it should be. 0.79.0 went to open testing with this open.
expected: A dragged exercise lands where the finger lets go, every time.
who: members who reorder exercises during a workout
how_often: about 2 in 5 drags on the owner-size test phone; unknown on real phones
fix_line: Reproduce on a phone of the owner's size, log the scroll and the held card's shift at the drop, then fix the drop place

title: Two server change files still say they are not live although the notes say both went live on 16 Nov
what: The first line of the direct-read record change and of the bell done-and-read change still says not applied live. The notes record both as applied on the live server on 16 Nov 2026. The feature map read those first lines and marks both server features as hidden, while the admin app side of the bell is marked live. Anyone who trusts the file line gets the wrong state.
expected: Each server change file says its true live state and date, as the two before them do.
who: anyone reading the code to learn what is live, and this audit's feature map
how_often: every time
fix_line: Change both first lines to say applied live with the date, after a check of the live migration list

title: The phone offers to install the watch app on old Wear OS watches that cannot install it
what: The owner's rule is that every watch card and pop-up shows only for a connected watch that can install the app. The notes say the install offer still shows for a Wear OS 2 watch, which the store refuses, because the phone cannot read a watch's Android version before the app is on it. A note appears only after the store refuses.
expected: The install offer shows only for a watch that can install the app, or it says up front which watches work.
who: members with an old Wear OS 2 watch
how_often: once per such member, at the install card
fix_line: Add a short line on the card saying which watches work, since the phone cannot read the watch's version

title: A watch update is easy to miss: the pop-up hides for a day on the back button and leaves no lasting sign
what: The owner saw the watch update pop-up once, closed it without tapping, and did not see it again over many opens. The notes say the Android back button counts as Later, which hides the pop-up for 24 hours, and that no lasting reminder exists, unlike the phone's own update line. The owner's idea of a lasting dot and an Update ready row is in the backlog, not built.
expected: A member who closes the pop-up can still see that a watch update waits, somewhere that stays.
who: members with the watch app
how_often: each watch app update
fix_line: Add a quiet dot on Settings and an Update ready row in the watch section

title: The Hindi half of the privacy notice does not mention the AI Assistant
what: The English privacy notice tells gym owners that what they type or say to the AI Assistant goes to Claude and Groq. The Hindi version on the same page was approved and published without that part: its list of outside companies still describes Claude as only answering help questions and Groq as only handling spoken feedback. The notes call this an old gap that was left because English wins.
expected: The Hindi version says the same things as the English one, including the AI Assistant.
who: owners who read the privacy notice in Hindi
how_often: every time
fix_line: Add the AI Assistant paragraph and the two company rows to the Hindi version, after he approves the Hindi words

title: The rest alert still decides 'does the watch have our app' from the one signal that was proven broken
what: The notes say every released watch app up to 0.78.0 never announced itself to the phone, and that the update pop-up, Update on watch and Install on watch were moved to a rule that uses several signals. The check that picks how the rest countdown is sent to a watch was left on the old single signal, as the notes admit. For a watch running one of those older watch apps the phone reads it as a watch without the MettleUp app.
expected: The rest alert uses the same several-signal rule as the watch update pop-up, so a watch with an older watch app is recognised.
who: members whose watch runs a watch app older than the fix
how_often: every rest, until the watch app is updated
fix_line: Make the rest alert's watch check use the shared several-signal rule

title: One smart app link 'everywhere', but the check-in poster page still tells iPhone users something different
what: The notes describe one smart link everywhere, with iPhone visitors told the iPhone app is coming soon and to keep the link. The check-in poster page was left out on purpose: an iPhone visitor there still reads that MettleUp is an Android app for now, with no word that an iPhone app is coming. The app link page and the gym invite page say one thing, the check-in page another.
expected: Every page a member can reach by link or poster tells an iPhone user the same thing.
who: iPhone users who scan the check-in poster
how_often: every time
fix_line: Give the check-in poster page the same 'iPhone app is coming soon' words, after he approves them

title: The notes treat the staff sign-in card in the member app as a live screen, but it is switched off
what: The notes list the staff door among the member app's mobile number boxes and check its promise that the PIN is never stored, as if members and staff can see it. Its switch is off, so the card never shows. The feature list also disagrees with itself: one row calls this hidden, another calls staff unlocking their gym with number and PIN live.
expected: The notes and the feature list say plainly that this card is off, and the row marked live is corrected or shown to have another way in.
who: gym owners and desk staff using the member app
how_often: every time
fix_line: Mark the staff sign-in card as switched off wherever it is described, or switch it on

title: Website says MettleUp staff cannot open a gym's member list unless the owner lets them in, but HQ has an emergency button that opens it without the owner
what: The gym-owner home page says, under 'Closed to our staff', that they cannot open the member list unless the owner lets them in for 1 hour. HQ has an 'Open in an emergency' button: MettleUp picks a reason, types a sentence, picks 15, 30 or 60 minutes, and the gym's records open read-only with no yes from the owner. The owner does see it afterwards, with the reason.
expected: Either the website says that MettleUp can open read-only access in an emergency and that the owner always sees it, or the emergency button needs the owner's yes.
who: gym owners reading the website
how_often: every visit to the home page
fix_line: Change the home page line to say MettleUp can open read-only access in an emergency and the owner sees every look, or remove the emergency button

title: Website says the AI sees columns only and never sees member details, but the AI is also shown up to 5 example rows from the gym's file
what: The home page card 'Import members with AI' carries the tag 'AI never sees member details' and the demo says 'AI · columns only'. The column matcher is sent the column names and up to 5 example rows of the file. Mobile numbers, emails and ID numbers are hidden and names and addresses are replaced by a placeholder, but the other cells of those rows (plan, fees paid, dates and any extra columns) do go to the AI company.
expected: The website says what is really sent: column names and a few example rows with phone numbers, emails, IDs, names and addresses hidden. Or only the column names are sent.
who: gym owners reading the website
how_often: every visit to the home page
fix_line: Reword the tag to 'AI never sees phone numbers or names', or send the column names only

title: Website says an AI credit is used only when the AI Assistant sends or saves something, but members' AI answers also use the gym's credits
what: The home page says 'A credit is used only when the AI Assistant sends or saves something' and the About page says 'You use AI credits only when the AI finishes a task for you'. The server also takes credits when members get an AI answer to a question: 10 answers use 1 credit, up to the owner's monthly limit. That charge is switched on. Neither page mentions it.
expected: The price pages name every way a credit is spent, including members' AI answers (10 answers = 1 credit) and the owner's switch to turn that off.
who: gym owners reading the website and About page
how_often: every visit; it costs credits each time members ask the AI
fix_line: Add one line to the home page and one row to the About page table: members' AI answers, 10 answers = 1 credit, owner can switch it off

title: Play listing draft says 'Back up to Google Drive', but the app no longer offers a Google Drive backup
what: The Play listing draft tells people they can back up to Google Drive or save one backup file. Since 4 Nov 2026 the app has one backup, the MettleUp account; Google Drive backup is no longer a choice. Only bringing back an OLD Drive backup is still there, and that card is marked for removal around Feb 2027. No screen starts a new Drive backup.
expected: The listing names the backup the app really has: the MettleUp account (sign in) or one backup file.
who: people reading the Play listing
how_often: every reader, if this draft is the live listing
fix_line: Change the listing line to 'Back up to your MettleUp account, or save one backup file you can keep'

title: Website says free messages go 'to everyone' and reach 'every member's app inbox', but only members who have joined in the app get them
what: The home page card is headed 'Free messages to everyone' and says the message reaches every member's app inbox; the AI Assistant demo says 'Send to 212 members', the same number as the whole imported member list. A free in-app message goes only to members who have installed the app and joined the gym in it. A member without the app gets nothing from it (the gym must use WhatsApp for them).
expected: The website says the free message reaches every member who has the app, or the demo numbers show fewer app members than members.
who: gym owners reading the website
how_often: every visit to the home page
fix_line: Change 'to everyone' to 'to every member with the app' in the heading, the card line and the price list

title: The founding-gym box still says 'When the AI Assistant comes', while the same page and the About page say it is here
what: The founding offer on the home page says 'When the AI Assistant comes, you also get 100 free AI credits every month'. The AI Assistant section higher on the same page presents it as available now, and the About page says founding gyms get 100 credits every month. A reader cannot tell whether the assistant is live.
expected: The founding box says founding gyms get 100 free AI credits every month, with no 'when it comes'.
who: gym owners reading the founding offer
how_often: every visit to the home page
fix_line: Replace the sentence with 'You also get 100 free AI credits every month', in English and Hindi

title: Website sells the shop, logo and colours, trainer plans, challenge and Your numbers as Pro only, but today every gym gets them: the pack switch is off
what: The price cards say Starter does not include the shop, the gym's logo and colours (also on the watch), trainer and diet plans, the monthly challenge, extra plan days and Your numbers. In the code the pack switch is off, so every gym, including one that pays for Starter, has all of them. The day the switch goes on, a paying Starter gym loses parts it has been using.
expected: Either the switch is on so the product matches the price cards, or there is a written plan to tell Starter gyms before the Pro parts close for them.
who: gyms paying for Starter
how_often: once, on the day the pack switch is turned on
fix_line: Decide the date to turn the pack switch on and warn Starter gyms first

title: Member website promises backup to your own Google Drive, but the app stopped Drive backup
what: The member website says in two places that the app backs up to the member's own Google Drive and brings it all back on a new phone. The app stopped making Google Drive backups on 4 Nov 2026: backups now go to a MettleUp account on MettleUp's server, and Drive is only there to bring back an old backup.
expected: The website names the backup the app really offers (sign in and keep workouts on a MettleUp account), or the Drive backup is brought back.
who: every visitor of the member website, and new members who look for the Drive backup
how_often: every time
fix_line: Change the two Google Drive lines (English and Hindi) to say the backup goes to a MettleUp account

title: Member website says an Apple Watch app is coming soon, but nothing for Apple Watch exists
what: The member website shows Apple Watch with a Coming soon tag and says We are working on them. No Apple Watch app or any work on one was found in the code.
expected: The website only says coming soon for something that is being built, or the Apple Watch lines are removed.
who: iPhone and Apple Watch owners who visit the member website
how_often: every time
fix_line: Remove the Apple Watch coming soon lines, or decide and plan the Apple Watch app

title: Member website says the iPhone app is coming soon while iPhone work is paused
what: The member website tells iPhone visitors the iPhone app is coming soon and that we are working on it. The iPhone build was paused by the owner on 5 Nov 2026 (Android first) and runs only when started by hand; nothing is published.
expected: The wording matches the real state, for example not on iPhone yet, until iPhone work starts again.
who: iPhone visitors of the member website
